reply.shortGloss: to close; to shut; to turn off
reply.emotion: matter-of-fact and helpful, reaching out to secure a room
notes: Cerrar is used for physical objects like doors and windows, but also for turning off electrical devices or water taps (e.g., cerrar la llave).
Do not confuse with terminar, which means to finish an activity or process rather than physically closing something.

senses.definition: Poner algo de modo que no esté abierto, impidiendo el paso o la entrada.

examples.text: Por favor, puedes cerrar la ventana.
examples.translation: Please, can you close the window.
examples.emotion: polite and direct, asking for a simple favor

senses.definition: Interrumpir el paso de un fluido o la corriente eléctrica.

examples.text: No olvides cerrar la llave del agua al terminar.
examples.translation: Don't forget to turn off the water faucet when you finish.
examples.emotion: helpful and practical, reminding someone of a household chore

senses.definition: Finalizar o concluir un negocio, un trato o un periodo.

examples.text: Vamos a cerrar el trato esta misma tarde.
examples.translation: We are going to close the deal this very afternoon.
examples.emotion: confident and decisive, sealing an agreement
